### J-1 CT-1 counts as named when only CT-10 is in the map
- quote: "not named in the component map's node labels"
- situation (adversary): a plan has CT-1 and CT-10, and the component map labels name only CT-10. The check is `c not in labels`, a plain substring test, so "CT-1" is found inside "CT-10" and no `component map misses CT-1` error is raised. The check exits 0 while CT-1 is missing from the map. With 10 or more contracts, CT-1 through CT-9 can each hide behind CT-10 to CT-19. Quoted text anywhere in the block also counts, including a `click` or `style` line or an edge label, so a "CT-3" outside a node label counts as a node label.
- fix: match whole IDs, for example `re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(c)}\b", labels)` or a `(?!\d)` lookahead, and take labels from node shapes only.
- validation: confirmed: explain.py line 112 tests `c not in labels` on a plain joined string, so "CT-1" matches inside "CT-10"; nothing else in the file matches whole IDs.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-22

### J-2 A path that resolves to a plan explainer but is spelled differently runs as topic mode
- quote: "a path resolving to `.nio/specs/<slug>/explainer.md` is plan mode, any other is topic mode"
- situation (adversary): `nio check explainer .nio/specs/x/../x/explainer.md`, an absolute path through a symlink, or `./.nio/specs/x/explainer.md` gives a `p` that is not resolved. The test `p == spec.path(...).parent / "explainer.md"` compares unresolved paths, and `target in {p.parent.name}` fails for a `.md` target. So `plan_mode` is false. The core-diagram, contract-ID, node-cap and walk checks are skipped, and the check exits 0 with `0 errors`. A path that merely resolves to the plan explainer is judged as a topic, and nothing says so.
- fix: compare `p.resolve()` with the resolved plan path.
- validation: confirmed: line 101 compares the unresolved `p` with the plan path, so a `..` or symlink spelling gives `plan_mode` False (a leading `./` is normalised by Path, but `..` and symlinks are not), although CT-4 says "a path resolving to" the explainer.
- disposition: fix-task by agent: fix task T-23

### J-3 Text in `> ` lines is outside the walk-through word cap
- quote: "`walk` is the section's text without fenced blocks, `![` lines, lines starting `> ` and the record lines of the Data model"
- situation (adversary): the 120-word cap and the "walk-through missing" check run on `walk`, which drops every line starting `> `. An explainer can put 2000 words of prose in blockquote lines under a diagram and still pass AC-36 with a short walk-through. The same drop means a section with only a quote and no real walk-through gives n=0 and fails. So the blockquote rule helps for the finish notes but is also a way to get under the cap.
- fix: strip only the `> Broken diagram:` and `> Images not rendered:` notes that `finish` writes, or cap the blockquote words as well.

### J-4 Only the first fenced block of a section is checked or rendered
- quote: "`fence` is the language of the section's first fenced block"
- situation (adversary): `sections` keeps `block` for the first fence only. A second block under the same heading, such as a 60-node Mermaid diagram or a syntax-broken one, is not node-counted and not rendered. `check` exits 0, even though AC-5 says "no diagram has more than 20 distinct node IDs". A first block labelled `Mermaid` or `mermaid title` is also not rendered, and nothing warns.
- fix: keep every block per section and run the cap and render over each, or fail a section that holds more than one diagram block.

### J-5 A plan without contracts.md passes the contract-ID check with no sign
- quote: "for each `### CT-n` in contracts.md (`implement.defs`) not named in the component map's node labels"
- situation (adversary): `check` reads contracts.md only `if ... exists() else []`. When the file is absent, renamed or empty, the list of contract IDs is empty. Every explainer then passes AC-6 without any ID in the map, and there is no note. AC-10 says the check still checks contract IDs when Node is absent, so a reader of `0 errors` assumes the IDs were checked. Contracts that only parse as `## CT-1` are also skipped without notice.
- fix: add a note, or an error, when plan mode finds no CT- items to check against.

### J-6 The host-format note is never printed
- quote: "render skipped: diagrams drawn with <format>"
- quote: "render skipped: Node is not installed"
- situation (consistency): `.nio/config.json` sets `{"explain": {"format": "excalidraw"}}` and the explainer has a component map and build order drawn as images. `nio check explainer checkout-refunds` runs. The only notes `check` can add are the two Node notes in `src/nio/explain.py`. On a machine with Node present, Mermaid blocks are rendered, and the output has no `render skipped: diagrams drawn with excalidraw` line. TC-35's first assertion (exit 0 with that line) fails, and the contract's notes rule is not met.
- fix: in `check`, when `fmt` is set and isn't `mermaid`, append `render skipped: diagrams drawn with <fmt>` to `notes` and keep rendering the Mermaid blocks, as CT-4 says.
- validation: ungrounded: TC-35 not defined by the spec or contracts

### J-7 The contract-ID reader is not the helper the spec names
- quote: "(`implement.defs`)"
- quote: "spec.items((p.parent / "contracts.md").read_text().splitlines()"
- situation (consistency): CT-4 says the `### CT-n` items of contracts.md are read through `implement.defs`. `src/nio/explain.py` calls `spec.items` on the raw lines of the file instead, so it skips `records.parse`, which `implement.defs` goes through. For the current fixtures the results agree, so the suite passes. The two readings can diverge if contracts.md's text is parsed differently by `records.parse` (for example, a front-matter block), and a later change to `implement.defs` would no longer reach the explainer check.
- fix: call `implement.defs(p.parent / "contracts.md")` and take its keys, as CT-4 names it, or change CT-4 to name `spec.items` if the raw read is the intent.

### J-8 The format note of CT-4 is not produced
- quote: "`render skipped: diagrams drawn with <format>` when `explain.format` is set and isn't `mermaid`"
- situation (correctness): with `explain.format` set to another format, `check` reads `fmt` but adds no such note, so notes hold only the Node and fetch cases.
- fix: after the loop, or before it, append `render skipped: diagrams drawn with {fmt}` in plan mode when `fmt != "mermaid"`. Add a test. If the note is for a later task, say so in the task.
- validation: refuted: tasks.md puts TC-35 (the host-format note) in T-16 of E-9, and T-4 serves only AC-9/AC-10 with TC-14/TC-15 (render and Node/fetch notes), so the format note is not part of E-2.

### J-9 Contract ID match is a substring test
- quote: "if c.startswith("CT-") and c not in labels"
- situation (correctness): with CT-1 and CT-10 in contracts.md, a map that labels only CT-10 passes for CT-1, because "CT-1" is a substring of "CT-10". The check then misses a contract the AC says must fail.
- fix: match with `re.search(rf"{re.escape(c)}(?!\d)", labels)`. Add a CT-1/CT-10 test.
